idea.title: Network Scanner — Scan local network for active devices and open ports

plan.tagline: Discover active devices and open ports on your local network in seconds.
plan.problem: Small businesses and indie developers waste hours manually checking network devices and ports using scattered tools like ping sweeps and port scanners.
plan.solution: A lightweight Python CLI that scans the local network, identifies active devices, lists open ports, and stores results in a local database for quick access and reporting.
plan.target_market: Indie hackers, developers, and small business owners who need a simple, offline-first network scanning tool without complex setups or cloud dependencies.
mvp_features: Scan local network for active IPs (ICMP ping sweep)
Detect open ports (TCP) with customizable range
Store results in SQLite database for historical tracking
Generate simple text/CSV reports of findings
--demo mode with hardcoded offline data for testing

build_phases.name: Core DB + add
build_phases.description: Implement SQLite schema for storing devices/ports and basic CLI commands (scan, add, list)

build_phases.name: Reports + alerts
build_phases.description: Add report generation (text/CSV) and basic alerting for new devices/ports

build_phases.name: Demo + polish
build_phases.description: Implement --demo mode with hardcoded data, refine --help, handle edge cases (e.g., no network)

plan.demo_script: Run `netsweep --demo` to see a simulated scan of 3 devices (192.168.1.1-3) with open ports 22, 80, 443. Results are saved to a local DB and displayed in a simple table.
plan.phuket_angle: Phuket co-working spaces and small hotels can use NetSweep CLI to quickly audit guest Wi-Fi networks for unauthorized devices or open ports, ensuring security without complex tools.
